title: The Classroom of Ordinary Life
headline: How Ordinary Moments Form Christlike Character
headline_sub: The Classroom of Christlikeness Is Ordinary Life
tagline: You don’t need a bigger platform to practice Christlikeness. You need today’s next act of obedience.
seo_title: How Ordinary Moments Form Christlike Character (Luke 16:10) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Most of life isn't lived in dramatic moments but in traffic, meetings and interruptions. A devotional for men on Luke 16:10 and small obedience.
verse_text: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much….

scriptures.text: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much….
And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus….

items: We often imagine spiritual formation happening in dramatic moments.
The enormous temptation.
The life-changing decision.
The leadership crisis.
Those moments matter.
But most of your life will not be lived there.
Most of your life will be lived in:
traffic,
meetings,
interruptions,
emails,
chores,
delays,
small frustrations,
someone receiving credit you thought you deserved,
your spouse asking something when you’re tired,
your child interrupting something you considered important,
the opportunity to exaggerate when nobody would know.
These moments don’t look spiritually significant.
But they are not empty.
Every ordinary moment is another opportunity to practice who you are becoming.
Patience or impatience.
Gratitude or entitlement.
Humility or self-importance.
Truthfulness or manipulation.
Forgiveness or rehearsal.
The classroom of Christlikeness is not somewhere you eventually arrive.
You are already sitting in it.

sections.label: We Want the Big Yes While Resisting the Small Yes

items: A man might say, “I would die for my family.”
Maybe.
But will you put the phone down when your child is talking?
Will you listen to your wife when you’re exhausted?
Will you apologize without immediately explaining why you did what you did?
Will you keep your word when breaking it would be easier?
Will you serve when nobody notices?
Will you give someone else credit?
We imagine heroic surrender while resisting ordinary surrender.
Your impulse can be real without becoming your instruction.
A life surrendered to Christ is often built through small yeses before it is tested through enormous ones.
